The main takeaway from our work is that
, if the underlying graph G is a random regular graph, then the expansion of the graph is robust against a certain number of edge faults.

, in the case where d is sufficiently large, the random regular graph with edge faults exhibits expansion through cores, i.e. there is a constant c>0 such that the probability that the random regular graph G with d vertices and edge fault parameter f contains a c-core of size at least c d is at most 1-2exp(-d).

, for any given graph, the random regular graph with the same degree and number of vertices is a robust model of the graph under edge faults: The probability that the graph remains connected is close to one, as long as the fault probability f is below the critical value f_c, where f_c is the probability that a random edge is absent from the random regular graph.
